newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan paper says Eritrean opposition killed 30.
newsitem.headline: Sudan paper says Eritrean opposition killed 30.

text.p: A Sudanese government newspaper said on Tuesday that Eritrean opposition forces had killed at least 30 soldiers in a series of attacks on Asmara's troops, which it said continued to mass on Sudan's borders.
Sudan accuses Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda of supporting attacks by Sudanese rebels which gained momentum last month in the south and east of Sudan. The three countries deny the charge.

The government-owned newspaper al-Ingaz al-Watani also renewed Khartoum's charge that Israel was involved, saying military aid including tanks and troop transport vehicles from the Jewish state was "continuing to flow into Asmara".

In its report on Tuesday, the newspaper said the Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) dealt "strong blows" to Eritrean forces in attacks which it said took place last month near the border with Sudan. The report could not be independently confirmed.
"The series of operations was executed by the engineering units of the Front in the period from January 21 to 24," the report said.
It said a landmine exploded in one attack west of the Eritrean town of Teseney, which lies near the Sudan border, killing 30 soldiers. It said a number of soldiers died in another landmine explosion.

The newspaper last week said the Eritrean opposition had killed 189 fighters belonging to the ruling Eritrean People's Liberation Front and the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army, the main Sudan rebel movement.
